summary:
National Guard troops continue to remain deployed in D.C. more than a year after their initial arrival, drawing scrutiny from civil liberties advocates, while statehood advocates are intensifying efforts ahead of the midterm elections and working to build support among state-level lawmakers. A U.S. senator has committed to prioritizing D.C. statehood, and advocacy organizations are framing the federal response to recent events as evidence of why local autonomy is needed.

Without statehood, D.C. does not control its own National Guard and cannot refuse the deployment of other states' troops within its borders.
